examples.blurb: A plate, a boss, a union and G1 rounds selected by geometry — the reference part.
examples.demonstrates: extrude, tool bodies, union, fillet with selectors, assert_watertight
examples.title: Boss plate

examples.blurb: A stepped section revolved about Z; exact planes, cylinders and rounded rims.
examples.demonstrates: path profiles, revolve, circular edge selection, fillet
examples.title: Revolved knob

examples.blurb: A rounded block hollowed from the top to a uniform wall.
examples.demonstrates: fillet on vertical edges, shell with an open face
examples.title: Shelled enclosure

examples.blurb: An L-bracket on the YZ plane with equal, two-distance and distance-angle chamfers.
examples.demonstrates: sketch planes other than XY, chamfer kinds, allow_empty
examples.title: Chamfered bracket

examples.blurb: A through bore whose exact rims are labelled, then rounded by that label.
examples.demonstrates: subtract, exact boolean rims, label_edge, labeled() selection
examples.title: Bored block

examples.blurb: A variable-radius round growing along one edge under a linear law.
examples.demonstrates: fillet radius laws
examples.title: Tapered fillet

examples.blurb: A pentagonal pyramid carved by five exact planes; its slant edges rounded with curvature continuity (g2), and the five rounds closed by the setback Gregory vertex cap with dual cross-jet corners.
examples.demonstrates: boolean carve with exact planes, chord-length edge selection, vertex blend cap
examples.title: Pyramid apex

examples.blurb: A block corner where rounds of three different radii meet, closed by the variational corner fit: three NURBS sectors certified G2.
examples.demonstrates: fillet_each radius groups, at_vertex edge selection, variational corner fit
examples.title: Mixed-radius corner

examples.blurb: Parameters, an expression and a named configuration drive a plate and its rib.
examples.demonstrates: param, param_expr, p(), expr(), configurations
examples.title: Parametric plate

examples.blurb: A printable two-body box: shelled base with screw bosses from a loop, a bar-lip lid with loop-cut vents, exact-cone countersinks and a vents-off configuration.
examples.demonstrates: loops computing placements, shell, multi-body documents, configurations suppressing loop features, chord_length_between
examples.title: Project box

examples.blurb: A deep-groove bearing assembly: races revolved with exact torus grooves and chamfered lead-ins, and one ball built once and placed eight times by trigonometry.
examples.demonstrates: assemblies (part, place, translate), revolve with arc paths, exact torus and sphere surfaces, trigonometric placement loops, product-structure STEP export
examples.title: Ball bearing

examples.blurb: A twenty-tooth spur gear whose flanks are true involutes computed in the script, bored and keyed in one combined cut.
examples.demonstrates: computed polygon profiles, script functions, boolean tool unions
examples.title: Involute gear

examples.blurb: Seven backswept blades carved by one star-shaped cut whose spiral walls and tapered trailing edges this script computes.
examples.demonstrates: script functions, computed star polygons, logarithmic spirals, single-cut cavities
examples.title: Centrifugal impeller

examples.blurb: The classic seven tabletop dice — d4, d6, d8, d10, d%, d12, d20 — with engraved Inter numerals (6 and 9 underlined, the d4 read at its corners), plus a rounded pipped d6. Every die is carved from a block by one plane cut per face pair and its edges chamfered.
examples.demonstrates: plane_at custom sketch planes, polygon profiles, engraving with counters, computed face normals and vertices, spherical dimple cuts, mitre-apex chamfers, multi-body sets
examples.title: Dice set

examples.blurb: Three springs from one verb: a ground-end compression spring, a tapered valve spring, and a left-hand spring phased a quarter turn — every path an exact rational helix.
examples.demonstrates: helical_sweep, exact helix paths, ground flat ends, taper_to, left_hand winding, start_angle phasing
examples.title: Coil spring

examples.blurb: Three lofted blades — stadium sections whose chord and pitch the script computes per station — twisted, phased 120° apart and unioned onto a revolved hub with a tapered nose.
examples.demonstrates: loft through computed sections, rational stadium profiles, rigid rotations, chart-wrapping boolean unions on closed lofted walls
examples.title: Marine propeller

examples.blurb: A shaft with a keyway cut by a moved and turned tool, and a chamfered lead-in.
examples.demonstrates: translate, rotate, subtract, chamfer on a circular edge
examples.title: Keyed shaft

examples.blurb: A 4:1 planetary set as an assembly — sun, one planet placed three times at its mesh phase, an internal ring gear cut by a toothed disc, and a spider carrier — whose involute teeth and planet phasing are all computed in the script.
examples.demonstrates: computed involute teeth, internal ring gears, meshing-assembly phasing, the (Zs+Zr)%N constraint, single-polygon spiders, assemblies (one part placed many times with rotate then translate)
examples.title: Planetary gearbox

examples.blurb: The smallest real-thread part: an M10×1.5 stud from one verb — a coarse, short coil that serves in seconds, with the tip left square for speed.
examples.demonstrates: threaded_rod, ISO thread designations, tip_chamfer option
examples.title: Threaded stud

examples.blurb: A single short M6 hex bolt — head, plain shank and a real modeled ISO thread from one verb, sized to build fast.
examples.demonstrates: bolt generator, thread_length, tip_chamfer option
examples.title: Hex bolt

examples.blurb: A plate with a flush exact-cone clearance seat and the flat-head M5 screw that fits it — one quick thread coil in the whole build.
examples.demonstrates: clearance_hole with countersink, countersunk head bolts, axis_at placement
examples.title: Countersunk joint

examples.blurb: An M6 hex bolt with its nut, a socket-head cap screw, and a countersunk screw as an assembly — the three screws are one parametric part family — with real modeled ISO threads, heads, tip lead-ins, and runout from the nominal tables.
examples.demonstrates: bolt and nut generators, ISO thread designations, head styles, printed-fit clearance, part families (one parametric part, several sizes)
examples.title: Fastener kit

examples.blurb: A wedge bracket with an M6 cap screw and washer threaded in normal to its inclined face, screwed down by two flat-head screws flush in countersunk holes through its flange.
examples.demonstrates: tapped_hole and clearance_hole on arbitrary axes, placing fasteners on hole axes (frame), thread phase, countersinks, assemblies
examples.title: Angled fitting

examples.blurb: A 76 butt hinge: two leaves with five knuckles, a separate pin, and three countersunk M3 screw holes a leaf, opened to 150°.
examples.demonstrates: hinge generators (butt), screw holes from a designation, sizes that follow the length, the open angle
examples.title: Door hinge

examples.blurb: A continuous hinge: 25 knuckles along 200, one comb cut a leaf whatever the count.
examples.demonstrates: hinge generators at high knuckle counts
examples.title: Piano hinge

examples.blurb: A straight flexure with rounded roots for flexible plastics, and a slotted serpentine that lets a rigid plate bend.
examples.demonstrates: living_hinge styles, single-profile construction
examples.title: Living hinges

examples.blurb: A shelled box and its lid joined by a print-in-place hinge grown out of their back walls along the seam.
examples.demonstrates: hinge_bodies on existing bodies, print-in-place pins, shells
examples.title: Hinged box

examples.blurb: A print-in-place hinge as an assembly: the leaves mated about the pin axis, the open angle a slider, and a swing check for the first collision.
examples.demonstrates: assembly hinges, mates driven by a parameter, limits, swing
examples.title: Hinge assembly

examples.blurb: The hinged box as an assembly: box and lid are separate parts hinged along their seam, and the lid opens on a slider without rebuilding either part.
examples.demonstrates: assembly seam hinges (a.hinge_bodies), mates on a literal axis, a driven open angle, swing
examples.title: Hinged case

examples.blurb: The three joint sizes of a six-axis arm (L, M, S), each a motor driving a cycloidal reducer: finned housing, slotted stator and windings, a rotor with 180°-opposed cams, two biarc-fitted cycloid discs riding the cams round the ring pins, output pins, and a cross-roller bearing with its rollers at ±45°. One slider per module turns the output; rotor, discs and roller cage follow it.
examples.demonstrates: computed cycloid flanks fitted with G1 biarcs (deviation checked against the backlash), revolute joints with followers at gear ratios, sub-assemblies, part appearance, finned castings with rounded roots
examples.title: Cycloidal joint modules

examples.blurb: A complete six-axis robot arm on its cycloidal joint modules: cast base and shoulder, tube links with flanged ends, wrist, an ISO 9409 tool flange and a parallel gripper, bolted together with real M5/M6 screws. Six joint sliders move the arm without rebuilding a part, the tube lengths rebuild their links, and the grip opens the jaws.
examples.demonstrates: revolute joints on sub-assembly axes, two-root links mated at a driven length, assembly-parameter drives, swing to first contact, interference, fasteners, part appearance
examples.title: Six-axis arm

examples.blurb: The boss plate as a project: plate, boss, rounds — each migration starts from the document the earlier ones built.
examples.demonstrates: projects, previous(), migrations
examples.title: Boss plate in three steps
